definitions.explanation: Using someone or something excessively or mercilessly, pushing beyond reasonable limits. Can refer to overworking people, straining the body, or wearing out equipment.

examples.japanese: {体|からだ}を{酷使|こくし}してはいけない。
{目|め}を{酷使|こくし}したせいで、{視力|しりょく}が{落|お}ちた。
examples.english: My eyesight deteriorated because I strained my eyes too much.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}{酷使|こくし}してきたエンジンが、ついに{壊|こわ}れてしまった。
examples.english: The engine, which had been used harshly for many years, finally broke down.

notes:
USAGE:
Used both as a noun and as a する verb ({酷使|こくし}する). Common objects of {酷使|こくし} include {体|からだ} (body), {目|め} (eyes), {声帯|せいたい} (vocal cords), and machinery. Always has a negative connotation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {体|からだ}を{酷使|こくし}する (to overwork one's body)
- {目|め}を{酷使|こくし}する (to strain one's eyes)
- {労働者|ろうどうしゃ}を{酷使|こくし}する (to overwork laborers)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {使|つか}い{過|す}ぎ: overuse — milder and more neutral than {酷使|こくし}, which implies cruelty or mercilessness
